question: Expenditure made by the government for the creation of physical or financial assets is known as _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital Expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Capital Expenditure is the expenditure that is made by the government to create physical or financial assets.
 
• This may include the construction of roads, bridges, buildings, equipment, etc.
 
• The purpose of capital expenditure is to create long-term assets that will lead to economic growth in the future.
 
• This expenditure plays an important role in the government budget and is necessary to strengthen the economic structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure**

 
 
• This is the expenditure incurred by the government for general administrative functions and services.
 
• It includes salaries, pensions, subsidies, and other administrative expenses.
 
• Revenue expenditure is intended to provide immediate services and not to create long-term assets.
 
 
 
• **Defence Expenditure**
 
 
• This expenditure is made for the maintenance and advancement of the military and defense services.
 
• It includes the salaries of soldiers, purchase of weapons, and expenses for military operations.
 
 
 
• **Subsidy Expenditure**
 
 
• This expenditure is made by the government to provide subsidies in various sectors, such as agriculture, food security, and fuel.
 
• Its purpose is to provide financial support to the poor and low-income groups.
 
 
 
• **Financial Assets**
 
 
• These are assets that are held by the government as investments, such as government bonds, stocks, etc.
 
• The purpose of financial assets is to provide financial stability and generate income from investments.
